title: Staffing, crew-size, equipment and hours rules in the agreements and codes
question: Which rules in the labor agreements and City codes fix how many people work, on what equipment and on what hours?
finding: 29 rule entries (29 distinct rules) across 5 bargaining units plus 4 Charter or Administrative Code sections. The firefighters' agreement fixes crews of one officer and three firefighters on engines and squads and one officer and four on trucks (in 5 of 5 full texts since 2018); the deputies' agreement carries a jail-by-jail minimum table; electrical and craft agreements set minimum crews for specific jobs.
how: 25 text patterns run over one agreement text per Board file (238 files, 36 units named as the download README names them), plus four code sections. First and last year are the years the adopting Board files were introduced; "persists" counts the unit's full agreement texts from the first year on that contain the clause.
limits: A pattern finds wording, not every rule: a clause worded differently, in a scanned page with no text, or in an agreement not adopted by the Board (Muni operators under the SFMTA Board) is missed. The full texts before 2018 for the fire and police units are not on disk, so "first seen" for those units means "first on disk". Each agreement was negotiated and adopted by the Board; the agreement provides its own reasons for several rules (safety, training, the 0800 and 2000 roll calls), and these rows describe the rules without judging them.
